chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Yahya al-Halbi, from Malik al-Juhni, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'O Malik! You are our Shia. Do you not see that you are exaggerating in our matter? Indeed, one cannot describe the attributes of Allah; so just as one cannot describe the attributes of Allah, similarly one cannot describe our attributes. And just as one cannot describe our attributes, similarly one cannot describe the attributes of the believer.'

Indeed, when a believer meets a believer and shakes his hand, Allah does not cease to look at them, and sins fall from their faces just as leaves fall from the tree, until they part. So how can one describe the attributes of one who is like that?

ai.seo_question: What is the theological significance of handshaking between believers in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the theological principle of 'la yuqdar' (inability to fully encompass) by drawing an analogy between the divine attributes, the Imams, and the believers, a key concept in Shia usul al-fiqh regarding the status of the Ahl al-Bayt. It further illustrates the metaphysical reality of social interaction, where the physical act of shaking hands becomes a conduit for divine gaze and the shedding of sins, reinforcing the spiritual weight of communal bonds in Shia tradition.
